Right: dfs_tree() keeps the edges the depth-first search discovered, which snake through the graph as one long path, A to B, D, F, E, and finally C (accent arrows); A-C and B-E are dashed. The tree has depth 5, against 3 for the BFS tree." width="100%"} Returns the tree (or, with `source=None`, the forest) a depth-first search builds, as a directed graph with an edge from each node to every node it discovered (see `dfs_edges()`). DFS trees tend to be long and narrow, in contrast with the short, bushy trees of `bfs_tree()`, and are a natural skeleton for maze-like or hierarchical structures. Nodes keep their IDs, labels and attributes; each tree edge copies the weight and attributes of the original edge it follows. Nodes the search does not reach are left out. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The root, as an integer ID or a string label. If `None` (default), build a forest covering every node. [depth_limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Do not go deeper than this many hops from each root. If `None` (default), there is no limit. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which way to follow edges on a directed graph: `"out"` (default), `"in"`, or `"all"`. Ignored for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new directed graph: the DFS tree or forest. The original graph is not modified. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist, `depth_limit=` is negative, or `mode=` is invalid. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} From a corner of a 3 x 3 grid, the DFS tree snakes through the grid as a single path, while the BFS tree branches out: ::: {#c1e7bdd4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec grid = ec.Graph().add_grid_2d(rows=3, cols=3) dfs_depth = len(grid.dfs_tree(1).dag_longest_path()) - 1 bfs_depth = len(grid.bfs_tree(1).dag_longest_path()) - 1 dfs_depth, bfs_depth ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (8, 4) ``` ::: :::
